newsitem.title: CHINA: China recognises new Zaire, eyes friendly ties.
newsitem.headline: China recognises new Zaire, eyes friendly ties.

text.p: China on Tuesday recognised victorious Zairean leader Laurent Kabila, saying it was willing to develop friendly relations with his new Democratic Republic of Congo.

"We are willing to develop friendly cooperation and relations with the new Zairean government under the...principle of peaceful co-existence," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing.
Following a seven-month civil war in Zaire, Kabila on Saturday changed the name of his country to the Democratic Republic of Congo and declared himself its leader.
Kabila acted as his guerrillas entered Kinshasa, a day after President Mobutu Sese Seko relinquished power and abandoned his capital.
Shen said China respected the will of the Zaireans and frowned on foreign interference.
"We respect the choice of the Zairean people and wholeheartedly wish stability could return as soon as possible," Shen said.
"We believe that a country's affairs should be decided by the country's people themselves," he said.
